message.content:
Sure! If you’re looking for a single appliance that can handle a chocolate‑cake batter from start to finish, here are a few popular “machine” options:

| Machine | How it works | Why it’s great for chocolate cake |
|---------|--------------|-----------------------------------|
| **Conventional electric oven** | Standard heating element + timer | Most people already own one; you can bake at the exact temperature (usually 350 °F/175 °C) and control the bake time precisely. |
| **Convection oven** | Adds a fan to circulate hot air | Even heat distribution means a more uniform rise and a crispier top without over‑browning the edges. |
| **Toaster oven** | Compact, quick‑heat unit | Ideal for small batches or when you don’t want to preheat a full-size oven. |
| **Smart oven (e.g., Panasonic Smart Oven, Breville Smart Oven Pro)** | Touchscreen controls + pre‑set programs | You can select “Cake” or “Bake” presets that automatically adjust temperature, time, and sometimes even add a “warm” mode after baking. |
| **Air‑fryer** | Uses rapid air circulation | Works surprisingly well for cakes—just set it to a low temperature (around 300 °F/150 °C) and watch the timer. |
| **Instant Pot® (with “Cake” setting)** | Pressure cooker + slow‑cook function | The “Cake” mode uses a reversible rack and a special “cake” setting that keeps the batter from sticking and gives a moist crumb. |
| **Electric cake maker / cake pan** | Dedicated cake‑baking appliance (often with a removable pan) | Some models come with a built‑in timer and temperature control, making it almost plug‑and‑play. |

### Quick tip
If you’re new to baking, start with a **conventional oven**—it’s the most forgiving. Once you’re comfortable, try a convection oven or a smart oven for a bit more automation and consistency.

Happy baking!
